newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee called to open little changed.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee called to open little changed.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures were called to open little changed on Wednesday, as traders expected the market to consolidate near current levels following the recent run-up to almost six-week highs.

New York arabica futures ended mostly firmer on Tuesday, but well off session highs. September rose 0.55 cent, to 188.90 cents, after ranging from 192.50 to 186.50. December ended 1.65 cents higher, at 166.05 cents, while the back months closed up 3.65 to down 0.25.
The September/December switch narrowed to 22.85 cents compared with 23.95 cents at the close on Monday.
Technically, traders said September faced resistance at 193.00-194.00 cents, followed by 200.00 cents. On the downside, a break below 184.50 cents could send September down toward 180.00 cents.
After Tuesday's close the CSCE reported certified coffee stocks fell by 304 60-kg bags as of July 28, to 91,774 bags. An additional 6,871 bags were pending grading, the exchange said.

On the weather front, U.S.-based forecaster Weather Services Corp said on Wednesday that there is no damaging cold weather expected during the next seven days in Brazil's coffee belt. Low temperatures will be in the 50s to low 60s F (low to middle teens C), WSC said, with some cooler conditions in the higher elevations.

London coffee futures were broadly lower and near the bottom of the day's range early Wednesday, pressured by producer selling. At the midday break, September was down $24, to $1,644, after ranging from $1,655 to $1,640. November fell $26, to $1,634.
